bluetooth: SetDiscoveryFilter Unit Test Add unit test coverage for the new API. Two mocking devices are created with different RSSI but same UUID. The test will proceed following test sequence. 1. Set a "tight" filter with high RSSI threshold, low pathloss tolerance, and only one UUID. Then start the discovery by first client. Expected Behavior: Both devices will blocked by this filter. 2. Update filter for the first client to be "classic_loose", which is a filter with low RSSI threshold, high RSSI tolerance, and no UUID requirement. Expected Behavior: Both devices will blocked by this filter. NewBlue should ignore this filter since it is for classic only. 3. Update filter for the first client to be "looser_rssi", which is a filter with lower RSSI threshold. Expected Behavior: The device with higher RSSI and correct UUID will be seen by the interface. 4. Send an empty filter by the first client to clear existing filter settings. Expected Behavior: The second device should be discovered. 5. Setup a "uuid" filter by the first client to look for a nonexistent UUID. Expected Behavior: Both devices will blocked by this filter. 6. Setup a "looser_rssi" with a correct uuid filter by second client. Expected Behavior: Both devices will blocked by this filter, since the second client has not requested discovery. Filter will not merge. 7. Start discovery by the second client. Expected Behavior: The device with higher RSSI will be seen by the interface. 8. Update filter for the first client to be "loose", which is a filter with low RSSI threshold, high RSSI tolerance, and no UUID requirement. Expected Behavior: The second device should be discovered. 9. Stop discovery by the first client. Expected Behavior: The filter should unmerge to become a "looser_rssi" which the second client holds. The device with higher RSSI will be seen by the interface. 10. Send an empty filter by the second client to clear existing filter settings. Expected Behavior: The second device should be discovered. biod: Do not emit error in log when checking EC command support When checking whether a specific EC command is supported, we use the EC command EC_CMD_GET_CMD_VERSIONS. autotest: cellular_Smoke: Ignore v6 DNS entries Cellular currently has v6 support disabled. If the DNS server we communicate with has AAAA entries for the hostname in question, a corresponding socket.getaddrinfo call would have some entries containing v6 server addresses. This change allows for cellular_Smoke to ignore v6 entries when calling CheckInterfaceForDestination. Note that doing this opens the possibility for FetchUrl to use a different physical interface to communicate with the server over v6. We can get away with this because cellular is the lowest priority physical interface, meaning that CheckInterfaceForDestination would fail if WiFi or ethernet could potentially be used. In the long-term, something like CL:1404384 would allow for the enforcement of either v4 or v6 for communication with the server and for CheckInterfaceForDestination.
